entries.prefix: This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the objectives and scope of the regulation, which aims to enhance the internal market for artificial intelligence while ensuring safety, fundamental rights, and innovation through specific rules and prohibitions related to AI systems in the Union.

This chunk outlines the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, detailing the entities and circumstances to which the regulation applies and the exceptions regarding military, national security, and scientific research purposes.

This chunk outlines the exclusions from the Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, specifying that it does not apply to pre-market AI research and development, personal use by individuals, certain consumer protection laws, and free and open-source AI systems unless they are classified as high-risk.

This chunk defines key terms related to AI systems, including 'AI system,' 'risk,' 'provider,' 'deployer,' 'authorised representative,' 'importer,' 'distributor,' 'operator,' 'placing on the market,' 'making available on the market,' 'putting into service,' 'intended purpose,' 'reasonably foreseeable misuse,' and 'safety component' for the purposes of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

This chunk defines key terms related to the operation, assessment, and regulation of AI systems, including instructions for use, recall and withdrawal of AI systems, performance, conformity assessment, and data used in training and validation.

This chunk defines various terms related to artificial intelligence, including types of data (testing, input, biometric, sensitive operational), identification systems (biometric identification, verification, emotion recognition), and the roles of law enforcement authorities.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 3 (Definitions), defines key terms related to law enforcement, AI governance, authorities, incidents, data types, profiling, testing plans, AI regulatory sandboxes, AI literacy, and real-world testing conditions.

This chunk defines key terms related to the testing of AI systems, including 'subject', 'informed consent', 'deep fake', 'widespread infringement', 'critical infrastructure', 'general-purpose AI model', 'high-impact capabilities', 'systemic risk', 'general-purpose AI system', 'floating-point operation', and 'downstream provider'.
The regulation mandates that AI system providers and deployers must ensure adequate AI literacy among their staff and users, tailored to their knowledge and the specific context of AI application.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 5, outlines various AI practices that are prohibited due to their potential to manipulate individuals, exploit vulnerabilities, unfairly classify or assess individuals, and infringe on privacy and rights, particularly in contexts such as criminal risk assessment and biometric categorization.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 5, outlines the conditions under which 'real-time' remote biometric identification systems may be used in public spaces for law enforcement, emphasizing strict necessity, specific objectives, and compliance with fundamental rights safeguards.

This chunk outlines the conditions under which 'real-time' remote biometric identification systems can be used for law enforcement in publicly accessible spaces, requiring prior authorization from a judicial or independent authority, with specific provisions for urgent situations and mandatory notifications to relevant authorities.

This chunk outlines the reporting requirements for Member States regarding the use of real-time remote biometric identification systems in public spaces for law enforcement, including the submission of annual reports to the Commission and the publication of aggregated data, while clarifying that these provisions do not override existing prohibitions under other Union law.

Article 6 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the criteria for classifying AI systems as high-risk based on their intended use as safety components of products or as standalone products subject to conformity assessments, along with additional conditions specified in Annex III.

This chunk outlines the process for the Commission to amend specific conditions related to high-risk AI systems while ensuring that such amendments do not reduce the protection of health, safety, and fundamental rights as established by the Regulation.

Article 7 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 empowers the Commission to adopt delegated acts to amend Annex III by adding or removing high-risk AI systems based on specific risk criteria related to health, safety, and fundamental rights.

This chunk outlines the compliance obligations for high-risk AI systems, emphasizing adherence to specific requirements based on their intended use and the integration of existing Union harmonisation legislation.

The chunk outlines the requirements for establishing, implementing, and maintaining a risk management system for high-risk AI systems, detailing the processes for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating risks throughout the system's lifecycle.

This chunk addresses the considerations providers must take into account regarding the potential adverse impacts of high-risk AI systems on individuals under 18 and other vulnerable groups when implementing a risk management system.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 10, outlines the requirements for the development and management of training, validation, and testing data sets for high-risk AI systems, emphasizing data quality, governance, bias detection, and compliance with fundamental rights.
This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 addresses the handling, retention, and processing justification of special categories of personal data in relation to bias correction in high-risk AI systems.

Article 11 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the requirements for the technical documentation of high-risk AI systems, including its preparation, content, and provisions for small and microenterprises to submit simplified documentation for compliance assessment.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 12, outlines the requirements for high-risk AI systems to automatically log events throughout their lifecycle to ensure traceability, facilitate monitoring, and record specific usage details.

This chunk outlines the requirements for transparency and information provision for high-risk AI systems, detailing the necessary instructions for use that must be provided to deployers, including system characteristics, performance metrics, risks, and oversight measures.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 14, outlines the requirements for human oversight of high-risk AI systems to ensure they are effectively monitored and that risks to health, safety, or fundamental rights are minimized during their use.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 15, outlines the requirements for high-risk AI systems to ensure accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle, including measures to address performance metrics, resilience against errors and unauthorized alterations, and the prevention of biased outputs and vulnerabilities.

This chunk outlines the obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems, including compliance with regulatory requirements, documentation, quality management, conformity assessments, and accessibility standards.

This chunk outlines the requirements for providers of high-risk AI systems to establish a documented quality management system that ensures compliance with the Artificial Intelligence Act, detailing necessary components such as regulatory compliance strategies, design and development procedures, risk management, and post-market monitoring.

Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 mandates that providers of high-risk AI systems retain specific technical and compliance documentation for ten years after the system's market introduction, ensuring availability for national authorities, even in cases of provider bankruptcy.

Providers of high-risk AI systems must maintain automatically generated logs for at least six months, in accordance with applicable Union or national laws, including those related to personal data protection.

This regulation mandates that providers of high-risk AI systems must take immediate corrective actions if they identify non-compliance with the regulation and inform relevant parties, including distributors and market surveillance authorities.

This chunk outlines the obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems to supply necessary information and documentation to competent authorities upon request, including access to system logs, while ensuring confidentiality of the obtained information.

This chunk outlines the requirements for providers of high-risk AI systems from third countries to appoint an authorised representative in the EU, detailing the representative's responsibilities, including compliance verification, documentation retention, and cooperation with authorities.
This chunk outlines the obligations of importers regarding the conformity, documentation, labeling, and cooperation with authorities for high-risk AI systems before they are placed on the market.

Article 24 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the obligations of distributors regarding the verification, compliance, and corrective actions for high-risk AI systems before they are made available on the market.

This chunk outlines the responsibilities of distributors, importers, deployers, and other third parties regarding high-risk AI systems, including their obligations when modifying or branding such systems, and the cooperation required with initial providers to ensure compliance with regulatory standards.

This chunk outlines the AI Office's authority to create and recommend voluntary model contract terms for high-risk AI system providers and their third-party suppliers, while ensuring compliance with intellectual property and confidentiality laws.

This chunk outlines the obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems, including ensuring compliance with usage instructions, assigning competent human oversight, monitoring system operations, managing input data relevance, maintaining logs, and informing workers about the use of such systems.

This chunk outlines the obligations of public authorities and Union institutions deploying high-risk AI systems, including registration requirements, data protection assessments, authorization for post-remote biometric identification, documentation of use, and annual reporting to relevant authorities.
Deployers of high-risk AI systems must inform individuals affected by these systems and cooperate with authorities regarding their implementation and oversight.

Article 27 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 mandates that deployers of high-risk AI systems conduct a fundamental rights impact assessment prior to deployment, detailing usage processes, affected individuals, potential risks, human oversight measures, and governance arrangements.

Article 28 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the responsibilities and requirements for Member States to establish notifying authorities that oversee the assessment and monitoring of conformity assessment bodies, ensuring objectivity, impartiality, and confidentiality in their operations.

This chunk outlines the application process and requirements for conformity assessment bodies seeking notification from the relevant Member State authority, including necessary documentation and compliance verification.

Article 30 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the notification procedure for conformity assessment bodies by notifying authorities, detailing the requirements for notification, the information to be included, and the process for addressing objections from the Commission or other Member States.

This chunk outlines the requirements for notified bodies under the Artificial Intelligence Act, including their establishment, independence, organizational structure, confidentiality, and professional integrity in conducting conformity assessments for high-risk AI systems.

This chunk outlines the requirements for notified bodies to possess adequate internal expertise and personnel, participate in coordination activities, and stay informed about relevant standards in relation to AI system evaluations.

This chunk outlines that a conformity assessment body is presumed to meet the requirements of Article 31 if it demonstrates compliance with relevant harmonised standards published in the Official Journal of the European Union.

Article 33 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the responsibilities and requirements for notified bodies regarding subcontracting tasks and the use of subsidiaries in conformity assessments, including the need for compliance with specific standards, accountability, provider consent, public disclosure of subsidiaries, and document retention for oversight.

Article 34 outlines the operational obligations of notified bodies in verifying the conformity of high-risk AI systems, ensuring minimal burdens on providers, and providing necessary documentation to the notifying authority.

Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 mandates the assignment of unique identification numbers to notified bodies and requires the Commission to maintain and publicly share an updated list of these bodies along with their respective activities.

Article 36 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the procedures for notifying changes to the designation of notified bodies, including requirements for informing authorities about cessation of activities, compliance failures, and the management of certificates during such changes.
This chunk outlines the conditions under which certificates for high-risk AI systems remain valid despite suspension, restriction, or withdrawal of designation by the notifying authority.

Article 37 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the Commission's authority to investigate the competence of notified bodies, the obligation of notifying authorities to provide relevant information, the confidentiality of sensitive information during investigations, and the procedures for corrective measures if a notified body fails to meet the required standards.

Article 38 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 mandates the Commission to facilitate coordination among notified bodies for high-risk AI systems and ensures that notifying authorities support their participation in this collaborative effort.

This chunk outlines the conditions under which conformity assessment bodies from third countries can be authorized to perform notified body activities in the EU, contingent on meeting specific compliance requirements.

Article 40 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the presumption of conformity for high-risk AI systems and general-purpose AI models with harmonised standards, the Commission's responsibilities for issuing standardisation requests, and the promotion of investment and innovation in AI through stakeholder engagement and alignment with international standards.

Article 41 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the conditions under which the Commission can adopt implementing acts to establish common specifications for AI system requirements and obligations when harmonised standards are not adequately provided by European standardisation organisations.

This chunk outlines the obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models regarding compliance with common specifications and the process for Member States to report deficiencies in these specifications to the Commission.
This chunk outlines the conditions under which high-risk AI systems are presumed to comply with specific regulatory requirements based on their training data and certification status.

Article 43 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems, detailing the options for compliance based on the application of harmonised standards or common specifications, and specifies the roles of notified bodies in the assessment process.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 43, outlines the conditions under which manufacturers of high-risk AI systems can opt out of third-party conformity assessments, the requirements for re-assessment after substantial modifications, and the Commission's authority to amend related annexes and procedures.

Article 44 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the requirements for certificates issued by notified bodies, including their language, validity periods, conditions for extension, and procedures for suspension or withdrawal based on compliance with AI system requirements.

This chunk outlines the information obligations of notified bodies regarding the communication of technical documentation assessments, quality management system approvals, and related activities to both the notifying authority and other notified bodies, while ensuring confidentiality.

Article 46 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the conditions under which market surveillance authorities can grant temporary derogations from conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems in exceptional circumstances related to public security, health, or environmental protection.

Article 47 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the requirements for providers to create and maintain an EU declaration of conformity for high-risk AI systems, ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and making it available to national authorities for a specified duration.

Article 48 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the requirements and conditions for affixing the CE marking on high-risk AI systems, including its visibility, digital accessibility, and the inclusion of the notified body's identification number.

Article 49 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the registration requirements for providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems in the EU database before these systems can be marketed or put into service.

The chunk outlines the transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems, requiring them to inform users when interacting with AI, mark AI-generated content, and disclose the use of emotion recognition or deep fake technologies, while specifying exceptions for law enforcement and artistic contexts.

This chunk outlines that the specified paragraphs do not alter existing transparency obligations under Union or national law for AI system deployers and discusses the AI Office's role in promoting codes of practice for detecting and labeling artificially generated or manipulated content, along with the Commission's authority to approve or establish common rules for these practices.

This chunk outlines the criteria for classifying general-purpose AI models as having systemic risk based on their impact capabilities and computational requirements, as well as the Commission's authority to adjust these criteria over time.

Article 52 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the notification procedure for providers of general-purpose AI models that meet certain criteria, including the assessment and potential designation of these models as presenting systemic risks by the Commission, as well as the process for reassessment of such designations.

This chunk outlines the obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models, including requirements for technical documentation, information sharing with AI system providers, compliance with copyright laws, and cooperation with authorities, while also detailing exceptions and the role of the Commission in standardization and confidentiality.

Article 54 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 mandates that providers of general-purpose AI models from third countries must appoint an authorised representative in the Union to ensure compliance with regulatory obligations before placing their models on the market.

This chunk outlines the obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, including model evaluation, risk assessment, incident reporting, cybersecurity measures, and compliance with codes of practice or harmonised standards.

Article 56 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the responsibilities of the AI Office in promoting and facilitating the development of codes of practice for AI, ensuring they address obligations related to systemic risks, stakeholder involvement, and regular monitoring and evaluation.

This chunk outlines the deadlines and procedures for finalizing codes of practice related to the implementation of obligations under the Artificial Intelligence Act, including the role of the AI Office and the Commission's authority to establish common rules if necessary.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 57, outlines the establishment and operation of AI regulatory sandboxes by Member States to foster innovation and ensure compliance with AI regulations, including provisions for cooperation, resource allocation, and guidance for participants.

This chunk outlines the objectives, operational guidelines, and supervisory roles of AI regulatory sandboxes established under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, including provisions for legal compliance, innovation support, data protection involvement, and liability considerations for participants.

This chunk outlines the responsibilities of national competent authorities regarding the establishment, reporting, and public accessibility of AI regulatory sandboxes, as well as the Commission's role in providing a centralized interface for stakeholder interaction and guidance.

This chunk outlines the Commission's responsibility to establish detailed arrangements for AI regulatory sandboxes, including eligibility criteria, application procedures, and operational guidelines to ensure uniformity and accessibility across the EU.

This chunk outlines the support and services available to prospective AI providers in regulatory sandboxes, including guidance on compliance, testing facilities, and the conditions for real-world testing to ensure fundamental rights and safety.

This regulation outlines the conditions under which personal data collected for other purposes can be processed in the AI regulatory sandbox to develop AI systems that serve substantial public interests, ensuring compliance with data protection laws and safeguarding the rights of data subjects.

This chunk clarifies that the provisions regarding the processing of personal data for developing AI systems in the public interest do not override existing Union or national laws that restrict such processing for other purposes or establish necessary legal bases for it.

This chunk outlines the conditions and procedures for testing high-risk AI systems in real-world conditions outside regulatory sandboxes, including the requirement for a real-world testing plan, approval from market surveillance authorities, and compliance with relevant laws.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 60, outlines the conditions and requirements for testing high-risk AI systems in real-world conditions, including data transfer safeguards, duration limits, protection for vulnerable groups, informed consent, oversight responsibilities, and incident reporting protocols.

This chunk outlines the obligations of AI system providers to notify national authorities about the suspension or termination of real-world testing and their liability for any damages incurred during such testing.

This regulation mandates that informed consent must be obtained from participants before testing AI in real-world conditions, ensuring they are fully informed about the testing's nature, conditions, their rights, and the identification details of the testing.

This chunk outlines the responsibilities of Member States and the AI Office to support SMEs and start-ups in accessing AI regulatory sandboxes, providing tailored training, facilitating communication, and considering their specific needs in regulatory processes.
Article 63 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines that microenterprises can simplify compliance with certain quality management system elements while still adhering to other regulatory obligations.
This chunk outlines the responsibilities of the Commission and Member States in supporting the AI Office to enhance Union expertise and capabilities in artificial intelligence.

This chunk outlines the establishment, composition, roles, and operational procedures of the European Artificial Intelligence Board, including the designation of representatives from Member States and the formation of sub-groups for cooperation on market surveillance issues.

Article 66 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the tasks of the Board, which include advising the Commission and Member States on the consistent application of the Regulation, coordinating national authorities, sharing expertise, providing implementation advice, and promoting AI literacy.

This chunk outlines the responsibilities of the Board in supporting national authorities with AI regulatory sandboxes, advising on guidance documents and international matters, and handling qualified alerts related to general-purpose AI models.

Article 67 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes an advisory forum to provide technical expertise and advice to the Board and the Commission, ensuring balanced representation from various stakeholders in the field of artificial intelligence.

Article 68 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes a scientific panel of independent experts to support the enforcement of AI regulations, detailing their composition, responsibilities, and the procedures for ensuring their impartiality and conflict of interest management.
This chunk outlines the provisions for Member States to access scientific panel experts for enforcement support, including potential fees and the Commission's role in facilitating this access.

This chunk outlines the responsibilities and requirements for Member States to establish national competent authorities and single points of contact for the implementation and oversight of the Artificial Intelligence Act, including their independence, resource adequacy, and communication obligations.

Article 71 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the creation and maintenance of an EU database for high-risk AI systems, detailing the responsibilities for data entry, accessibility, and compliance with privacy regulations.

This chunk outlines the requirements for providers of high-risk AI systems to establish a documented post-market monitoring system and plan that ensures ongoing compliance and performance evaluation throughout the AI system's lifecycle.

Article 73 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 mandates that providers of high-risk AI systems must report serious incidents to market surveillance authorities within specified timeframes, depending on the severity of the incident and any established causal links.

This chunk outlines the reporting requirements for serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems that are safety components of devices, specifying the notification process to national authorities and the Commission.

This chunk outlines the application of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 to AI systems, the reporting obligations of market surveillance authorities, the designation of relevant authorities for high-risk AI systems, and the enforcement powers of these authorities in relation to market surveillance and compliance with Union law.

This chunk outlines the responsibilities and powers of market surveillance authorities in the EU regarding high-risk AI systems, including their coordination with other authorities, access to necessary documentation and source code, and the independence of judicial authorities.

This chunk outlines the powers and responsibilities of the AI Office and market surveillance authorities in monitoring, supervising, and ensuring compliance of general-purpose AI systems, particularly those classified as high-risk, under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

This chunk outlines the powers and responsibilities of market surveillance authorities in overseeing real-world testing of AI systems to ensure compliance with the regulation, including the ability to suspend or modify testing based on serious incidents or non-compliance.

Article 77 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 grants national public authorities the power to access documentation related to high-risk AI systems to ensure compliance with fundamental rights, mandates the identification and public listing of these authorities by Member States, allows for testing requests if documentation is insufficient, and establishes confidentiality obligations for the obtained information.

Article 78 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the obligation for the Commission, market surveillance authorities, and other involved parties to maintain the confidentiality of sensitive information and data obtained during the regulation's implementation, while outlining specific protections for intellectual property, public security, and the conduct of legal proceedings.

This chunk outlines the procedures for national market surveillance authorities to evaluate and address AI systems that present risks to health, safety, or fundamental rights, including compliance assessments, corrective actions, and notifications to relevant bodies.

This chunk outlines the procedures for national market surveillance authorities to address non-compliance of high-risk AI systems with regulatory requirements, including the notification process and the imposition of restrictive measures.

This chunk outlines the procedures for market surveillance authorities to evaluate AI systems classified as non-high-risk by providers, including actions to ensure compliance if the systems are found to be high-risk, and the consequences for providers who fail to take corrective actions.

Article 81 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the Union safeguard procedure for evaluating objections raised by market surveillance authorities regarding national measures on AI practices, including the Commission's role in consultation and decision-making on the justification of such measures.

Article 82 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the responsibilities of market surveillance authorities and operators regarding high-risk AI systems that, despite compliance, pose risks to health, safety, fundamental rights, or public interest, requiring corrective actions and communication among Member States and the Commission.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 83, outlines the obligations of market surveillance authorities in Member States to address formal non-compliance by AI system providers regarding CE marking, EU declarations of conformity, registration, and technical documentation, and the subsequent measures to restrict or withdraw non-compliant systems from the market.

This chunk outlines the designation of Union AI testing support structures by the Commission to perform specific tasks related to AI and to provide independent technical or scientific advice as needed.

This regulation allows individuals or entities to file complaints with market surveillance authorities if they believe there has been a violation of the Artificial Intelligence Act, ensuring these complaints are considered in market surveillance activities.

Article 86 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 grants individuals affected by decisions made using high-risk AI systems the right to receive clear explanations regarding the AI's role in the decision-making process, while noting exceptions based on Union or national law.
This chunk addresses the applicability of Directive (EU) 2019/1937 to the reporting of infringements of the Regulation and the safeguarding of individuals who report these infringements.

This chunk outlines the exclusive supervisory and enforcement powers of the Commission regarding Chapter V of the Regulation, delegating implementation to the AI Office while allowing market surveillance authorities to request assistance from the Commission.

Article 89 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the AI Office's authority to monitor compliance with the regulation by general-purpose AI model providers and establishes the process for downstream providers to lodge complaints regarding alleged infringements.

This chunk outlines the process by which the scientific panel can issue a qualified alert to the AI Office regarding potential systemic risks posed by general-purpose AI models, including the necessary information to be provided in such alerts.

Article 91 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the Commission's authority to request documentation and information from providers of general-purpose AI models to assess compliance, including the procedures for such requests and the responsibilities of the providers.

Article 92 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the AI Office's authority to conduct evaluations of general-purpose AI models to ensure compliance and assess systemic risks, including the appointment of independent experts and the procedures for accessing necessary information.

This chunk outlines the Commission's authority to request compliance measures from AI model providers in response to systemic risks, including the implementation of mitigation strategies and potential market restrictions.

This chunk establishes that Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies similarly to providers of general-purpose AI models, while allowing for more specific procedural rights outlined in the current regulation.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 95, outlines the encouragement and facilitation by the AI Office and Member States for the development of voluntary codes of conduct aimed at applying specific requirements to AI systems, excluding high-risk ones, while considering ethical guidelines, environmental sustainability, AI literacy, inclusivity, and the protection of vulnerable groups.

This chunk outlines the Commission's responsibility to create guidelines for the practical implementation of the Artificial Intelligence Act, addressing various articles, prohibited practices, transparency obligations, and the relationship with Union legislation, while considering the needs of SMEs and relevant standards.

Article 97 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the conditions under which the European Commission can adopt delegated acts, including the duration of delegation, the process for revocation by the European Parliament or Council, the requirement for expert consultation, notification procedures, and the conditions for the acts to enter into force.

Article 98 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes that the Commission will be supported by a committee as defined in Regulation (EU) No 182/2011, with specific reference to the application of Article 5 of that regulation.

This chunk outlines the rules and conditions for penalties and enforcement measures imposed by Member States for violations of the Artificial Intelligence Act, including specific fines for non-compliance with various provisions, while considering the interests of SMEs.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 99, outlines the factors to consider when imposing administrative fines for infringements, the rules for applying these fines to public authorities, and the procedural safeguards and reporting requirements for Member States.

This chunk outlines the conditions and procedures under which the European Data Protection Supervisor can impose administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices, and agencies for non-compliance with the Artificial Intelligence Act, including factors influencing the fine amount and the rights of the parties involved.

Article 101 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the conditions under which the Commission can impose fines on providers of general-purpose AI models for various infringements, specifying the maximum fine limits, the process for determining fines, and the rights of the providers during the proceedings.

This chunk specifies that when implementing technical specifications and procedures for security equipment related to Artificial Intelligence systems, the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 must be considered.

This chunk specifies that when adopting delegated acts related to artificial intelligence systems classified as safety components, the requirements from Chapter III, Section 2 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 must be considered.

This chunk specifies that when adopting delegated acts related to safety components of Artificial Intelligence systems, the requirements from a specific section of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 must be considered.

This chunk adds a paragraph to Article 8 of Directive 2014/90/EU, stating that the Commission must consider the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 when dealing with AI systems that are safety components.

This chunk specifies that when creating delegated and implementing acts related to safety components of Artificial Intelligence systems, the requirements from a specific section of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 must be considered.

This chunk specifies that when creating delegated acts related to safety components of Artificial Intelligence systems, the requirements from a specific section of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 must be considered.

This chunk outlines amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139, specifying that when adopting implementing and delegated acts related to Artificial Intelligence systems classified as safety components, the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 must be considered.

This chunk specifies that when implementing acts are adopted for safety components of artificial intelligence systems, they must consider the requirements outlined in Chapter III, Section 2 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

This chunk adds a new point to Annex I of Directive (EU) 2020/1828, referencing Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, which establishes harmonized rules on artificial intelligence and amends several existing regulations and directives.

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 111, outlines compliance deadlines for AI systems and general-purpose AI models already on the market, specifying requirements for bringing them into alignment with the Regulation by set dates based on their market introduction.

Article 112 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines the Commission's obligations to annually assess and report on the need for amendments to AI regulations, evaluate the functioning of the AI Office, and review various aspects of AI governance and standardization every four years.

This chunk outlines the responsibilities of the Board, Member States, and national authorities in providing information to the Commission for evaluations and reviews, the Commission's obligation to consider various stakeholders' positions, the potential for regulatory amendments based on technological developments and impacts of AI, the development of an evaluation methodology by the AI Office, and the requirement for a comprehensive assessment of the Regulation's enforcement by 2031.
This chunk outlines the entry into force and application dates of the Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, specifying when different chapters and articles will take effect.

This chunk lists various Union harmonisation legislation directives and regulations related to machinery, toys, recreational craft, lifts, explosive atmospheres, radio equipment, pressure equipment, cableway installations, personal protective equipment, and appliances burning gaseous fuels.

This chunk lists various Union harmonisation legislation, including regulations and directives related to medical devices, civil aviation security, vehicle approval, marine equipment, rail interoperability, and motor vehicle market surveillance.

This chunk covers the type-approval requirements for motor vehicles and their trailers, focusing on general safety and the protection of vehicle occupants and vulnerable road users, as well as common rules in civil aviation related to unmanned aircraft and their components.

This chunk lists various serious criminal offences, including terrorism, human trafficking, sexual exploitation of children, drug trafficking, and others, as referenced in Article 5(1) of the Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

Annex III of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 identifies high-risk AI systems across various sectors, including biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, and law enforcement, as specified in Article 6(2).

This chunk of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 outlines high-risk AI systems used by law enforcement and public authorities for purposes such as polygraph testing, evidence evaluation, risk assessment, profiling, migration management, and supporting judicial processes.
This chunk outlines the required contents of the technical documentation for AI systems, including descriptions of the system's purpose, interactions, development processes, and compliance measures.

This chunk outlines the requirements for technical documentation related to validation, testing, monitoring, risk management, and compliance of AI systems as specified in Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Annex IV.
This chunk outlines the required contents of the EU declaration of conformity for AI systems, including identification details, provider information, compliance statements, and relevant standards.

This chunk outlines the steps involved in the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control, including compliance verification of the quality management system, examination of technical documentation, and consistency checks of the AI system's design and development process.

This chunk outlines the conformity assessment procedure for AI systems based on the evaluation of the provider's quality management system and technical documentation, detailing the requirements for application, assessment, and maintenance of these systems.

This chunk outlines the procedures and requirements for notified bodies to assess the technical documentation and conformity of high-risk AI systems, including the need for additional evidence or testing, access to training models, issuance of assessment certificates, and the handling of changes affecting compliance.

This chunk outlines the requirements for AI system providers to grant notified bodies access to their premises and necessary information for periodic audits and potential additional testing of the AI systems.

This chunk outlines the information that providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems must submit and maintain up to date for registration under Article 49 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, including details about the provider, the AI system, its intended purpose, and its market status.

This chunk outlines the required information for the registration of high-risk AI systems, including contact details of the submitter, the AI system's EU database URL, and summaries of fundamental rights and data protection impact assessments.

This chunk outlines the required information for registering high-risk AI systems regarding real-world testing, including identification details, provider information, system description, testing plan characteristics, and any suspension or termination updates.

This chunk covers the regulations related to the Schengen Information System and the Visa Information System, including their establishment, operation, and use in the context of border checks, police cooperation, and judicial cooperation in criminal matters.

This chunk covers various EU regulations related to large-scale IT systems for managing biometric data, entry/exit information, travel authorizations, and criminal records of third-country nationals and stateless persons for purposes of law enforcement and border control.

This chunk covers two regulations from May 2019 that establish frameworks for interoperability between EU information systems related to borders, visas, police and judicial cooperation, asylum, and migration.

This chunk outlines the required technical documentation for providers of general-purpose AI models, detailing the information that must be included regarding the model's description, development process, training data, evaluation strategies, and system architecture, tailored to the model's size and risk profile.

This chunk outlines the required technical documentation for providers of general-purpose AI models, detailing the model's description, acceptable use policies, integration methods, development process, and data used for training and validation.
